prompt: According to the first verse of the Bible, what did God create in the beginning?
explanation: Genesis opens with God creating the heaven and the earth.

prompt: Eastward in what place did God plant a garden for Adam?
explanation: The Lord planted a garden eastward in Eden.

prompt: Who gave names to the cattle, the fowl, and every beast of the field?
explanation: The animals were brought to Adam to see what he would call them.

prompt: What was Abel's occupation?
explanation: Abel was a keeper of sheep, while Cain was a tiller of the ground.

prompt: Which son did Eve bear after the death of Abel?
explanation: Eve named her son Seth, appointed instead of Abel.

prompt: According to Genesis, how many years did Methuselah live?
explanation: All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years.

prompt: Which of these was NOT one of Noah's three sons?
explanation: Noah's sons were Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

prompt: Of what wood was Noah told to make the ark?
explanation: The Lord told Noah to make an ark of gopher wood.

prompt: How long did it rain upon the earth during the Flood?
explanation: The rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.

prompt: Upon which mountains did the ark rest?
explanation: The ark rested upon the mountains of Ararat.

prompt: What did the dove bring back to Noah in its mouth?
explanation: The dove returned with an olive leaf plucked off.

prompt: What token did God set in the cloud as a sign of His covenant with Noah?
explanation: God set His bow in the cloud as a token of the covenant.

prompt: What was the city with the great tower called, because there the Lord confounded the language?
explanation: The name of it was called Babel because the Lord confounded the language there.

prompt: From which city did Terah take Abram to go into Canaan?
explanation: Terah took Abram and went forth from Ur of the Chaldees.

prompt: Which king of Salem brought forth bread and wine to Abram?
explanation: Melchizedek king of Salem was the priest of the most high God.

prompt: What did Abram give Melchizedek?
explanation: Abram gave Melchizedek tithes of all.

prompt: What was the name of the son Hagar bore to Abram?
explanation: Hagar bore Abram a son and he called his name Ishmael.

prompt: To what was Abram's name changed?
explanation: God said his name would be Abraham, a father of many nations.

prompt: What new name did God give to Sarai, Abraham's wife?
explanation: God told Abraham that Sarai's name would be Sarah.

prompt: What did Lot's wife become when she looked back?
explanation: She looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt.

prompt: How old was Abraham when Isaac was born?
explanation: Abraham was an hundred years old when Isaac was born.

prompt: To which land was Abraham told to take Isaac to offer him?
explanation: God told Abraham to go into the land of Moriah.

prompt: What did Abraham offer in place of Isaac?
options: A ram caught in a thicket
explanation: Abraham offered a ram caught in a thicket by its horns.

prompt: Who came out to the well with a pitcher on her shoulder when Abraham's servant prayed?
explanation: Rebekah came out with her pitcher upon her shoulder.

prompt: Which twin came out holding Esau's heel?
explanation: Jacob was born with his hand on Esau's heel.

prompt: For what did Esau sell his birthright to Jacob?
explanation: Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles for his birthright.

prompt: In his dream at Bethel, what did Jacob see reaching to heaven?
explanation: Jacob dreamed of a ladder set up on the earth that reached to heaven.

prompt: What name did Jacob give the place where he dreamed of the ladder?
explanation: He called the name of that place Beth-el; it was first called Luz.

prompt: How many years did Jacob serve for Rachel before the first marriage?
explanation: Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed but a few days.

prompt: Whom did Laban give to Jacob in place of Rachel?
explanation: In the morning, behold, it was Leah.

prompt: After wrestling until daybreak, what new name was Jacob given?
explanation: His name would be no more Jacob, but Israel.

prompt: What did Jacob (Israel) make for Joseph?
explanation: Israel loved Joseph and made him a coat of many colours.

prompt: For how many pieces of silver was Joseph sold to the Ishmeelites?
explanation: His brothers sold Joseph for twenty pieces of silver.

prompt: Who bought Joseph in Egypt?
explanation: Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, bought Joseph.

prompt: Pharaoh's dreams foretold seven years of plenty followed by seven years of what?
explanation: Joseph said seven years of plenty would be followed by seven of famine.

prompt: What did Joseph have put in the mouth of Benjamin's sack?
explanation: Joseph's silver cup was put in the sack's mouth of the youngest.

prompt: In what land of Egypt did Israel dwell?
explanation: Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the country of Goshen.

prompt: Who named Moses?
explanation: Pharaoh's daughter called his name Moses, because she drew him out of the water.

prompt: Whom did Moses marry in Midian?
explanation: Jethro (Reuel) gave Moses his daughter Zipporah.

prompt: In what did the angel of the Lord appear to Moses on Horeb?
options: A flame of fire out of a bush
explanation: The bush burned with fire and was not consumed.

prompt: Who was appointed to be a spokesman for Moses to the people?
explanation: The Lord said Aaron would be Moses' spokesman unto the people.

prompt: What did Aaron's rod become before Pharaoh?
explanation: Aaron cast down his rod and it became a serpent.

prompt: What happened to the waters of the river in the first plague?
explanation: All the waters in the river were turned to blood.

prompt: What kind of lamb was to be used for the Passover?
options: A female of the third year
Without blemish, a male of the first year
A black lamb of the second year
explanation: The lamb was to be without blemish, a male of the first year.

prompt: How did the Lord cause the Red Sea to go back?
options: By the rod alone, without wind
explanation: The Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night.

prompt: What did the house of Israel call the bread from heaven?
explanation: The house of Israel called the name thereof Manna.

prompt: How many years did Israel eat manna?
explanation: The children of Israel did eat manna forty years.

prompt: Who held up Moses' hands so Israel would prevail against Amalek?
explanation: Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, one on each side.

prompt: Whose counsel led Moses to appoint rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens?
explanation: Jethro counseled Moses to appoint able men to help judge the people.

prompt: What is the first of the Ten Commandments in Exodus 20?
options: Thou shalt have no other gods before me
Honour thy father and thy mother
explanation: The first commandment: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

prompt: Which commandment carries the promise that thy days may be long upon the land?
options: Honour thy father and thy mother
explanation: Honouring parents is tied to long days upon the land.

prompt: What did Aaron make from the people's golden earrings?
explanation: Aaron fashioned the gold into a molten calf.

prompt: How long was Moses with the Lord on the mount when he wrote the words of the covenant?
explanation: Moses was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights.

prompt: Leviticus 19:18 commands Israel to love whom as themselves?
explanation: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

prompt: Which two spies came from the tribes of Judah and Ephraim?
explanation: Caleb of Judah and Oshea (Joshua) of Ephraim were among the twelve spies.

prompt: What did the spies carry between two on a staff from the brook Eshcol?
explanation: They bare a branch with one cluster of grapes between two upon a staff.

prompt: What did Moses set upon a pole so those bitten could look and live?
explanation: Moses made a serpent of brass; whoever beheld it lived.

prompt: Whose donkey (ass) spoke to him?
explanation: The Lord opened the mouth of the ass, and she spoke to Balaam.

prompt: Deuteronomy 6:5 says to love the Lord with all thine heart, all thy soul, and all thy what?
explanation: Love the Lord with all thine heart, soul, and might.

prompt: From which mountain did Moses view the promised land before his death?
explanation: Moses went up unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah.

prompt: In whose house did the two spies lodge in Jericho?
explanation: The spies came into a harlot's house named Rahab and lodged there.

prompt: What was Rahab to bind in her window?
explanation: The spies told her to bind the line of scarlet thread in the window.

prompt: What happened when the priests bearing the ark stepped into the Jordan?
options: The waters stood up and were cut off
explanation: The waters from above stood and rose up upon an heap.

prompt: On the seventh day, how many times did Israel compass Jericho?
explanation: On the seventh day they compassed the city seven times.

prompt: Who declared, "As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord"?
explanation: Joshua said, choose you this day whom ye will serve.

prompt: Which prophetess judged Israel?
explanation: Deborah, a prophetess, judged Israel at that time.

prompt: With how many men did the Lord say He would save Israel through Gideon?
explanation: By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you.

prompt: What did Samson reveal as the secret of his strength?
options: He prayed seven times a day
No razor had come upon his head
explanation: Samson told Delilah that there had not come a razor upon his head.

prompt: Who said, "Whither thou goest, I will go"?
explanation: Ruth said this to her mother-in-law Naomi.

prompt: Whom did Ruth marry?
explanation: Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife.

prompt: What did Hannah name the son she asked of the Lord?
explanation: Hannah called his name Samuel, because she had asked him of the Lord.

prompt: How did young Samuel respond when the Lord called him the final time?
explanation: Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.

prompt: Which tribe was Saul, the first king of Israel, from?
explanation: Saul's father Kish was a Benjamite.

prompt: Samuel taught that to obey is better than what?
explanation: To obey is better than sacrifice.

prompt: When choosing a king among Jesse's sons, the Lord said He looks on what?
explanation: Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.

prompt: How many smooth stones did David choose out of the brook?
explanation: David chose him five smooth stones out of the brook.

prompt: From which Philistine city was Goliath?
explanation: Goliath was of Gath.

prompt: Whose soul was knit with the soul of David?
explanation: The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David.

prompt: Bath-sheba was the wife of whom?
explanation: Bath-sheba was the wife of Uriah the Hittite.

prompt: Which prophet told David, "Thou art the man"?
explanation: Nathan said to David, Thou art the man.

prompt: What did Solomon ask the Lord to give him?
explanation: Solomon asked for an understanding heart to judge the people.

prompt: How many years did Solomon take to build the temple?
explanation: So was he seven years in building it.

prompt: Which queen came to prove Solomon with hard questions?
explanation: The queen of Sheba came to prove him with hard questions.

prompt: What brought Elijah bread and flesh by the brook Cherith?
explanation: The ravens brought him bread and flesh morning and evening.

prompt: To which city was Elijah sent where a widow would sustain him?
explanation: Elijah was sent to Zarephath, where a widow would sustain him.

prompt: On which mount did Elijah gather the prophets of Baal?
explanation: Elijah gathered Israel and the prophets of Baal unto mount Carmel.

prompt: What consumed Elijah's sacrifice, the wood, and even the water on Carmel?
explanation: The fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice.

prompt: After the wind, earthquake, and fire, how did the Lord speak to Elijah?
explanation: After the fire came a still small voice.

prompt: How did Elijah go up into heaven?
explanation: Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

prompt: What did Elisha ask of Elijah before he was taken?
options: A double portion of his spirit
explanation: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit.

prompt: How many times was Naaman told to wash in the Jordan?
explanation: Elisha told Naaman to wash in Jordan seven times.

prompt: Naaman was captain of the host of which king?
explanation: Naaman was captain of the host of the king of Syria.

prompt: How old was Josiah when he began to reign?
explanation: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign.

prompt: What did Hilkiah the high priest find in the house of the Lord in Josiah's day?
explanation: Hilkiah found the book of the law in the house of the Lord.

prompt: In Ezra 1, which king of Persia proclaimed that a house of the Lord should be built at Jerusalem?
explanation: Cyrus king of Persia made a proclamation to build the house of the Lord.

prompt: Nehemiah served as cupbearer to which king?
explanation: Nehemiah took up wine and gave it to king Artaxerxes.

prompt: In how many days was the wall of Jerusalem finished under Nehemiah?
explanation: The wall was finished in fifty and two days.

prompt: Who raised Esther?
explanation: Mordecai brought up Hadassah (Esther), his uncle's daughter.

prompt: Who asked Esther, "Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?"
explanation: Mordecai sent this message to Esther.

prompt: Who was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai?
explanation: They hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.

prompt: In what land did Job live?
explanation: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job.

prompt: Who declared, "I know that my redeemer liveth"?
explanation: Job testified that his redeemer liveth.

prompt: How does Psalm 23 begin?
options: Make a joyful noise unto the Lord
The heavens declare the glory of God
Bless the Lord, O my soul
explanation: Psalm 23 begins, The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.

prompt: According to Psalm 119:105, God's word is a lamp unto my feet and what?
explanation: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

prompt: Proverbs 3:5 counsels to trust in the Lord with all thine heart and lean not unto what?
explanation: Lean not unto thine own understanding.

prompt: Ecclesiastes says there is a season for every purpose under what?
explanation: To every thing there is a season, a time to every purpose under the heaven.

prompt: Who answered the Lord, "Here am I; send me"?
explanation: Isaiah answered the Lord's call, Here am I; send me.

prompt: In Isaiah 7:14, what is the name given to the son the virgin would bear?
explanation: A virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

prompt: Isaiah 53:6 says "All we like" what "have gone astray"?
explanation: All we like sheep have gone astray.

prompt: Jeremiah was told the Lord knew him and ordained him a prophet before when?
options: Before he was formed in the belly
explanation: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.

prompt: Jeremiah compared Israel in the Lord's hand to what in the potter's hand?
explanation: As the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand.

prompt: What filled the valley in Ezekiel's vision in chapter 37?
explanation: The valley was full of bones.

prompt: What did Daniel ask to be given to eat instead of the king's meat?
explanation: Daniel asked for pulse to eat and water to drink.

prompt: What name was given to Daniel by the prince of the eunuchs?
explanation: Daniel was given the name of Belteshazzar.

prompt: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, of what was the head of the great image made?
explanation: The image's head was of fine gold.

prompt: How many men did Nebuchadnezzar see walking in the fiery furnace?
explanation: He saw four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire.

prompt: What words did the hand write on the wall at Belshazzar's feast?
explanation: The writing was MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.

prompt: Into what was Daniel cast for praying to his God?
explanation: They cast Daniel into the den of lions.

prompt: What did the Lord prepare to swallow up Jonah?
explanation: The Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah.

prompt: How long was Jonah in the belly of the fish?
explanation: Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

prompt: To which great city was Jonah sent to preach repentance?
explanation: Jonah went unto Nineveh according to the word of the Lord.

prompt: According to Micah, from which town would come the ruler in Israel?
explanation: Out of Beth-lehem Ephratah shall come forth one to be ruler in Israel.

prompt: In Malachi 3, the people are told they have robbed God in what?
explanation: Wherein have we robbed thee? In tithes and offerings.

prompt: Whom did Malachi say the Lord would send before the great and dreadful day of the Lord?
explanation: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet.

prompt: Whom did Pharaoh give to Joseph as his wife?
explanation: Pharaoh gave Joseph Asenath, the daughter of Poti-pherah.

prompt: When Jacob blessed Joseph's sons, whom did he set before the elder Manasseh?
explanation: Jacob set Ephraim before Manasseh.

prompt: How many wives (princesses) did Solomon have?
explanation: Solomon had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines.

prompt: What affliction came upon King Uzziah until the day of his death?
explanation: Uzziah the king was a leper unto the day of his death.
